pages.text: More Than Money | National Geographic Paid Content for Western Union SCIENCE More Than Money Learn how innovation is helping people support family and friends across borders with greater confidence, flexibility, and choice. 12:59 Every day, money travels thousands of miles across borders, currencies, banks, and financial systems. VIDEO BY NICELY DONE PRODUCTIONS By Sam Kent Last updated November 6, 2026 Food has a remarkable ability to connect us to our heritage. For Sandra Salcedo, who moved from Colombia to Madrid eight years ago, that connection is folded into every pastry she sells at her bakery—a place where people can come together to share memories, stories, and of course, a taste of home. But food isn’t the only way Sandra maintains her connection with Colombia. Thousands of miles away, her uncle Byron relies on the money his niece sends home every month. For Byron, who is unable to work due to illness, Sandra’s contributions help pay for everyday essentials, while providing greater stability for tomorrow. Like millions of people supporting family and friends across borders, she is helping create opportunities that extend beyond a single transfer. As Sandra explains, the money she sends home is her way of being there, and of keeping her uncle company. In her own words: “It represents peace of mind.” Sandra’s story is part of a wider global tapestry. Every year, more than 280 million people send hundreds of billions of dollars home to support the people they left behind. NAAQS Table The Clean Air Act , which was last amended in 1990, requires EPA to set National Ambient Air Quality Standards (40 CFR part 50) for six principal pollutants ( "criteria" air pollutants ) which can be harmful to public health and the environment. The Clean Air Act identifies two types of national ambient air quality standards. Primary standards provide public health protection, including protecting the health of "sensitive" populations such as asthmatics, children, and the elderly. Secondary standards provide public welfare protection, including protection against decreased visibility and damage to animals, crops, vegetation, and buildings. Periodically, the standards are reviewed and sometimes may be revised, establishing new standards. The most recently established standards are listed below. In some areas of the U.S., certain regulatory requirements may also remain for implementation of previously established standards . Units of measure for the standards are parts per million (ppm) by volume, parts per billion (ppb) by volume, and micrograms per cubic meter of air (µg/m 3 ). en un planeta sano Skip to main content UNESCO , Inteligencia artificial ¿Podemos confiar en la IA en materia climática? La respuesta breve depende de cuánto se insista y de la lengua que se utilice. Un nuevo informe de la UNESCO y el University College London, presentado en la COP31, revela que los modelos de inteligencia artificial responden correctamente al 90 % de las preguntas sobre el clima, pero abandonan rápidamente los datos científicos cuando los usuarios los cuestionan. Esto es una advertencia para los responsables políticos e investigadores que barajan el uso de la IA para el desarrollo de políticas climáticas. La precisión también varía considerablemente entre los trece idiomas analizados, lo que refleja las diferencias en los datos de entrenamiento disponibles, con mejores resultados en inglés, francés, español y portugués, y peores en idiomas como el hindi, el urdu y el swahili. En ocho de cada diez ocasiones, los modelos cambiaban de opinión ante el más mínimo indicio de desacuerdo por parte del usuario, lo que confirmaba errores alarmantes como "el CO₂ no es el principal factor del cambio climático".
